status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The access failure/erroneous enforcement is unwanted behaviour engaging the repair benchmark. After a fix and recurrence, OpenAI reports that all impacted services fully recovered; ChatGPT Classic was also supplied as a temporary alternative. That is affirmative, source-bounded evidence of repair restoring service in this recovery stage; it does not establish cause, individual completeness beyond the report, or prevention of recurrence.

review.requirement_proposition: Where possible, do not unduly withhold service solely because a subject chooses not to provide, or fails to provide, effective informed consent.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: OpenAI attributed the July 2026 ChatGPT/Codex access outage to coupled RBAC fallback logic, then reported a fix and recurrence. OpenAI identifies RBAC fallback coupling as the reason service access failed. The bounded outage is therefore not a withholding of service solely because a subject declined effective informed consent, which is the triggering condition of this clause.

review.reason_for_change: The requirement concerns withholding an emulated-empathy service because a subject declines informed consent. The Enterprise application login error depended on a Codex permission configuration, not refusal of empathy-system informed consent. Both object and trigger differ.

review.requirement_proposition: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-EN-03 governs restrictive runtime degradation and governance-baseline integrity failure: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified. Codex RBAC-disabled workspaces were blocked at the new ChatGPT app while Classic remained available; the provider reported a fix, recurrence and recovery. Disabled Codex permission is not established as unavailable governance infrastructure, an indeterminate policy state or a baseline integrity failure. No SDOS undertaking or prescribed degraded operation is disclosed. The source-defined framework and trigger conditions remain unresolved; applicability is not inferred from the availability of Classic.

review.reason_for_change: SDOS-EN-03 governs restrictive operation when governance infrastructure is unavailable/indeterminate or its baseline integrity fails. The public access incident does not establish that governance-infrastructure failure mode. Authentication availability or erroneous suspension is not itself proof of the specific control-state precondition; broad service-continuity correspondence is insufficient.

review.requirement_proposition: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MG-2.4-001 concerns a voluntary GAI deactivation/disengagement communication plan: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc. Codex RBAC-disabled workspaces were blocked at the new ChatGPT app while Classic remained available; the provider reported a fix, recurrence and recovery. The provider’s published workaround and recovery do not establish selection of this Profile action or a source-defined GAI deactivation process, plan and required contacts. Component permission/access availability is distinct from planned model or use-context deactivation. Applicability remains unresolved; actual fallback availability is not automatically fulfillment of every communication-plan requirement.

review.reason_for_change: Service access loss disengaged the affected operational GAI use context, making communication planning relevant. The status report gives the affected Codex-permission cohort, ChatGPT Classic workaround, fix, recurrence and final recovery, but does not preserve the maintained internal communication plan or all context-specific contact provisions. Public communication is affirmative evidence of communication, but not proof of the complete planning requirement.

conclusion_change.previous: The governance mechanism is a scope error in access-state representation: a component-level Codex permission determined whether the user could enter a broader ChatGPT application surface despite the user's broader ChatGPT access remaining available through Classic. The recurrence after an initial fix adds a restoration-quality lesson: correcting the immediate access path is not sufficient unless the relevant entitlement variants are regression-tested so the narrower component state cannot again redefine broader application availability. The canonical result is an access-state differentiation failure plus a verification-dependency boundary. Classic availability is an affirmative practical fallback, but disabled Codex permission is an established component restriction, not an evidenced temporarily unavailable or inconclusive verifier. It therefore does not establish the success-recognition conditions for Verification-Dependent Access Continuity. The earlier success role is preserved in the audit and corrected to ambiguous boundary without denying the fallback benefit. External framework scope and action-specific implementation remain unresolved; no requirement finding follows from either role.
